title: DSC 106 Lab 0: Setup
description: In this lab, we will prepare our local environment for the course labs and assignments. We recommend you follow this guide step by step, but if you are already familiar with some of the tools, feel free to skip ahead.

title: DSC 106 Lab 1: Introduction to the Web platform
description: In this lab, we will learn: How does the Web work? What happens when I enter a URL in my browser and hit Enter? What languages are used to create webpages, what is each for, and what are their differences? How to write good HTML? How do CSS and JS look like, and how do we include them in our HTML? How can we create our own webpage and publish it on the Web?

title: DSC 106 Lab 2: Styling with CSS
description: In this lab, we learned the core concepts of CSS, how to use CSS selectors to target HTML elements, the difference between absolute and relative units, how to customize fonts, colors, and layouts, and how CSS resolves conflicting style declarations.

title: DSC 106 Lab 3: Introduction to JS
description: In this lab, we learned the basics of JavaScript, fundamental programming concepts, JavaScript and JSON data types, how to select and manipulate DOM elements, how to dynamically create and add elements to a webpage, and how to respond to user interactions using events.

title: DSC 106 Lab 4: JavaScript II
description: In this lab, we learned how to organize code using modular JavaScript, dynamically manipulate the DOM and use template literals to generate content, and fetch and display API data to create a more interactive user experience.

title: DSC 106 Lab 5: Visualizing categorical data with D3
description: In this lab, we learned about SVG and D3, how to create pie charts, build reactive visualizations for changing data, create interactive visualizations that update displayed data, and make visualizations accessible to users.

title: DSC 152 Lab 1: Introduction to R
description: In this lab, we learned the basics of R for statistical data science, including creating vectors, matrices, and dataframes, selecting elements and columns, using loops and random sampling, and writing functions that work with individual values or entire vectors.

title: DSC 152 Lab 2: Type I Error Rate and Power
description: In this lab, we will continue working with R to explore the concepts of Type I Error rates and Statistical Power.

title: DSC 152 Lab 3: Effect Size, A/B Testing
description: In this lab, you will investigate why a small p-value does not necessarily mean a large or useful effect. Then you will build a permutation test and use simulation to compare its power with a two-sample t-test.

title: DSC 152 Lab 4: Statistical Inference in Linear Models
description: In this lab, you learned how to perform statistical inference in linear models, interpret regression coefficients, test hypotheses about relationships between variables, and understand how to draw conclusions from regression results.

title: DSC 152 HW 1: One Sample Type I Errors and PowerDataset (TSV)
description: This homework is worth 30 points and covers Lectures 1–4 and Labs 1–2.

title: DSC 80 Final Project: Recipe Rating Prediction and Analysis
description: In this project, I'm working with the Recipes and Ratings datasets to analyze what types of recipes tend to have higher average ratings.
